article_core: The 1892 expedition was one phase of a distributed Harvard-Hosterwitz reference-production system. Field selection was governed by ecological and seasonal availability, the existing Harvard collection, access regime, desired biological state, preservation medium, body/time/route constraints and a remotely administered budget. Botanical institutions could compress access while wild excursions extended it. Cambridge sent collection-state priorities, money and route decisions outward while receiving reports and reference packets inward. Returned material became workshop stock whose members waited on taxonomic closure, priority and capacity before staged reactivation into later glass shipments. Finished models then entered separate mounting, packing, customs, receiving, repair and installation chains.

gate_B.principle: The expedition returned as stock, not as a shipment plan. Retention in 1892 did not imply immediate or eventual glass conversion.

governance_lanes.collection_state: Existing Harvard representations can make a local plant redundant; later desiderata/syllabus evidence shows how gaps and redundancies can be externalized into portable selection information.

governance_lanes.communication: Letters and telegrams move field status, patron instructions, collection needs and exceptional route decisions between Cambridge and the travelling party.

working_claims: The collection travelled twice: through objects moving to Cambridge and through portable descriptions of what Cambridge still lacked.
The expedition returned as stock, not as a shipment plan.
Botanical gardens compressed botanical access; field excursions extended it.
A jar, a boarding arrangement, and a railway diversion belonged to the same operational budget because each changed what Rudolf could turn into a usable reference.

Harvard governed the expedition without directing it minute by minute: it maintained balances, transmitted priorities, authorized facilities and answered exceptional route decisions while Rudolf and Ganong retained local discretion.
